info.name: VELOCITY-AI — Pipeline Runs (REST + SSE)
info.description: Each Runs > <pipeline> folder is fully self-contained end to end: login, discovery (including picking a template/theme for PPT and Prototype before launch), launch (POST /api/runs, prompt lives in the request body's "message" field), watch it live over SSE in two legs (before and after answering the clarify questionnaire -- verified live that answering before the pause actually arms is silently dropped), resolve gates, and inspect results/artifacts. Auth/Agents/Capabilities/PPT/Prototype/User Workflows folders are standalone quick-reference copies of the same discovery calls. Import the sibling environment file and select it before running anything -- it already carries the seeded local QA login.

item.name: 4. Launch  (the prompt lives in the "message" field of this request's body)
5. Watch Events (SSE) — part 1, until clarify  ★ open in Postman's Stream view

request.description: Attaches to the live stream right after launch. Every pipeline here has clarify.mode: auto, so it ALWAYS pauses at questionnaire_ready (after workflow_validated -> planner_start -> planner_complete -> gate_status) before any agent runs. This request stays open/blocked until you stop it -- verified live that answering too early (before this pause is actually armed) is silently dropped, so you must let this request reach questionnaire_ready first. In the Postman app: watch it arrive, then cancel this request and move to the next one. Running via Newman: pass --timeout-request 10000 (or similar) so it's aborted automatically once the pause has had time to arm -- that's expected, not a bug.

Send this only AFTER questionnaire_ready has actually arrived on the stream above (or after that request's timeout, which gives it enough time to arm) -- answering earlier is silently dropped, verified live.

item.name: 7. Watch Events (SSE) — part 2, until completion  ★ open in Postman's Stream view

request.description: Re-attaches AFTER answering. A fresh GET replays everything durable from the start (so you still see workflow_validated through questionnaire_complete), then continues live through agent execution to a terminal event (pipeline_complete/pipeline_failed/pipeline_cancelled/budget_aborted/error). domain-analyst -> epic-architect -> story-estimator -> nfr-specialist -> backlog-reviewer -> backlog-compiler run in this window.
Distinct from the live SSE stream above — a plain GET returning the durable event log so far. Useful to confirm what actually happened even if a Watch request above timed out.
Chains a child revision run off {{runId_userStories}} — send this AFTER the run above has completed.

item.description: Open-agent / arbitrary agent composition. Two examples: (A) pipeline_type "custom" with explicit agent_ids from the custom pool; (B) a BASE pipeline (user_stories) with a cross-pipeline agent spliced in. Fully self-contained.

Reference sub-folder plus one FULLY SELF-CONTAINED launch->watch(SSE)->answer->watch->inspect use case per pipeline -- each includes its own Login and Discovery (agent list, plus template/theme selection for PPT and Prototype) so it can be run top-to-bottom on its own, mirroring tools/api/runs/run.<pipeline>.http step for step.
